question.text: This company, based in Amsterdam, was given a monopoly on Dutch spice trade in 1602 and was one of the first major international corporations.
question.answerHtml: Dutch East India Company [accept United East Indian Company]
question.clue: Members of this group waterboarded and executed English merchants in the Amboyna massacre.

swap.text: The conflict spread when Germany attacked this neutral country hoping to capture Liege ("leezh") and outflank the French. Instead, Britain entered the war on the Allied side.
swap.clue: During WWI, this country stalled Germany at the Battle of Liege after being invaded as part of the Schlieffen Plan.

question.text: Charles didn't have much trouble ruling this modern day nation, but his successor Philip II did. This nation was the site of the 80 Years War and William the Silent helped lead its independence movement.
question.clue: An Ottoman import briefly triggered insanely high prices for tulips in this nation, where power rested with the stadtholder.

swap.leadin: Adam Hochschild wrote a book titled for this king's Ghost.
swap.text: Name this Belgian king who personally owned the Congo Free State. The atrocities of this king's Force Publique against the Congo's people resulted in him being forced to turn it over to the Belgian government in 1908.
swap.clue: Those lands had been gained for this man after he sent Henry Morton Stanley to negotiate with tribal chiefs.

question.leadin: Commoners from this region collected 500 pairs of spurs from defeated French nobles during the Battle of the Golden Spurs.
question.text: Name this part of Northern Europe where the early modern wool trade flourished. Philip IV (the fourth) of France attempted to cement control of this region in a war from 1297 to 1305.
question.answerHtml: Flanders [or Flandre; or Vlaanderen; prompt on Belgium; prompt on Belge; prompt on the Low Countries]
question.clue: A shibboleth was used here prior to the Battle of the Golden Spurs, and parts of the "race to the sea" occurred here, ending after the opening of the sea-locks during the Battle of the Yser.

swap.text: During the Eighty Years' War, this Dutch stadtholder ["shtaht-holder"] was assassinated by Balthasar Gerard, becoming the first head of state to be killed by a handgun.
swap.answerHtml: William the Silent [or William I, Prince of Orange, Count of Nassau; or Willem I; or Willem de Zwijger; prompt on William of Orange]
swap.clue: This leader's main antagonist dubbed this person a "pest on the whole of Christianity" and offered a massive bounty on this person's head, which led to the first assassination of a head of state with a firearm.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the military accomplishments of European dukes.
question.text: The Duke of Alba established the "Council of Blood" during this war, the revolt of the Spanish Netherlands against Philip II of Spain.
question.clue: The first assassination of a head of state by handgun was carried out by Balthasar Gerard during this war.

swap.leadin: In September of 1944, over 40,000 allied paratroopers were dropped near Arnhem in the Netherlands in an ambitious plan to end World War 2 by Christmas.
swap.text: Name this failed operation. Its success depended on the taking and holding of several bridges.
swap.clue: It was the last attempt to win the war by Christmas and had a strategic objective of forcing a crossing of the at .

question.text: This Flemish city saw half of its population flee in 1585 when the brutal "Spanish Fury" looted its besieged buildings and killed thousands of residents.
question.clue: Echoing Rome, the people of this city affixed the letters SPQA to its pioneering Beurs building.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the decline of cavalry warfare in Europe.
swap.text: This 1302 battle showed the superiority of pike-wielding Flemish militia against heavily armored French cavalry. Its name derives from the expensive equipment taken from the armor of the slain.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of the Golden Spurs [accept Battle of Courtrai or Battle of Kortrijk]
swap.clue: Stories of folk heroes who fought in this battle, such as the Cistercian lay brother Willem van Saeftinghe ("VILL-uhm vahn SAHF-ting-uh") and the weaver Pieter de Coninck, are romanticized in a novel by Hendrik Conscience ("kon-s'YAWNSS").

question.leadin: John Rooney and Jean Stengers published a study that contradicted nationalists of this ethnicity's claims of bourgeois corruption during one revolution.
question.text: What people's namesake region in Belgium is symbolized by a black lion on a yellow background? These people speak Dutch, unlike the Francophone Walloons.
question.clue: For the point, what surname is shared by the discoverer of penicillin, Alexander?

swap.text: The Eighty Years War was sparked by a rebellion led by William the Silent, a member of this Dutch royal house.
swap.clue: Previous members had been princes of its namesake city as well as staathalters.

question.leadin: After this meeting, Hugo Grotius was sentenced to life imprisonment, but escaped thanks to his mistress smuggling him out of prison in a book chest.
question.text: Name this 1618 to 1619 synod in the Netherlands convened to settle the Arminian controversy. This meeting saw disputes between the Arminians and followers of Franciscus Gomarus, as well as the condemnation of Johan von Oldenbarnevelt.
question.answerHtml: Synod of Dort [or Synod of Dordt or Synod of Dordrecht]
question.clue: Moderated by Bogerman, it set forth the doctrines of perseverance of saints, irresistible grace, total depravity, limited atonement, and unconditional election.

swap.leadin: Women called snaars were lower class citizens in this city, where residents declared allegiance by giving the Short Declaration.
swap.text: Name this setting of a massacre of Chinese citizens in 1740. This city was built on land captured from the Banten ("BAHN-tun") Sultanate.
swap.clue: Overseas officials based in a city with this name extracted cash crops through the Cultivation System and appointed trading directors for Dejima.

question.text: This woman was the queen of the Netherlands during the war. She fled to Great Britain during the occupation and broadcast messages of inspiration to the Dutch resistance movement.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the Netherlands.
swap.text: Since the Low Countries are actually low in altitude, these structures are built facing the ocean to keep the country from flooding. Modern ones are made of clay, though they were originally earthen.
swap.answerHtml: dikes [or levees; prompt on embankments; prompt on walls; do not accept “dams”]
swap.clue: This structures that enclosed reclaimed polders managed by water boards in the Dutch Republic.

question.text: Ludvigsen was influenced by the Provo movement, which passed urbanist "White Plans" in this non-Danish city. This city's own squatters movement was involved in its 1980 coronation riots.
question.clue: A failed 1650 attack on this city, where wealthy regents like the Bicker brothers held power, preceded a 22-year vacancy of leadership ending in the "Disaster Year."

swap.text: The Rampjaar also included this indecisive battle off of East Anglia, in which de Ruyter held off the combined but disorganized fleet of the Duke of York and the Comte d'Estrees.

question.text: The Wreckage of Eight Years of Purple was written by this openly gay, Islamophobic Dutch businessman, who founded a party known as his namesake "List." Shortly before the 2002 general election, this man was assassinated by environmental activist Volkert van der Graaf.

swap.leadin: This action was caused when unpaid mercenaries decided to loot the central city and it stiffened Dutch resistance, hastening the signing of the Pacification of Ghent.
swap.text: Name this 1576 massacre often referred to as the Spanish Fury.
swap.clue: Otto Oberstein, drowned in the Scheldt while retreating from it, and the five thousand troops under the Marquis de Havre mostly failed to offer any resistance.
